text:
alex: Heads-up — the quant-8 canary hitting worker-pool-12 started seeing OOMs around 08:12 UTC, ~15% of requests. Heap RSS climbs steadily with long-context prompts.
maria: ugh. any logs or OOM killer traces? can you paste dmesg and ps output? :eyes:
alex: pasted dmesg snippet and a small ps dump, link: https://internal/heapshots/1967/canary_dump.txt
alex: ```
[  1234.567890] Out of memory: Kill process 4321 (inference) score 987 or sacrifice child
[  1234.567891] Killed process 4321 (inference) total-vm:123456kB, anon-rss:98765kB
```
samir: ping — i'll try to grab a heapshot but don't recycle the canary yet. is this only after quant rollout?
alex: yes, fp16 canary was stable. this started immediately after the quant artifact went live.
prashant: quick hypothesis: quantized kernels change allocation patterns -> slab retention increases. could be smallalloc fragmentation or retained kv-cache pages.
maria: can we get jemalloc stats and smaps from the top process? MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true maybe. also grep for "madvise" or munmap failures in logs.
alex: running jemalloc stats now, will post. also seeing many small anonymous mmaps in smaps.
ci-bot: canary auto-snapshot scheduled: heapshot-1967000123-1 queued by @alex
samir: started heapshot with --alloc-sample=500 and perf-record on the same instance. I'll stream results. please avoid redeploy.
prashant: also check kv-cache reserved slab growth: prefix-cache sizes might keep pages pinned after quant decoding paths.
maria: if it's allocator fragmentation, try enabling aggressive background defrag flag on one canary: --alloc-defrag=aggressive and compare. want me to flip it?
alex: yes please flip on a single canary. i'll run traffic split 5% to it.
infra-bot: traffic-split applied: pool=worker-pool-12, variant=defrag-1, weight=5%
maria: also please set MALLOC_CONF=lg_dirty_mult:16,lg_chunk:22 on that instance so we get different free lists. not for all pools, just experiment.
samir: heapshot and perf data here: https://internal/profiles/1967000123/; initial glance shows many short-lived allocations ~1-4KB stacking up in tcache bins.
prashant: that's consistent with smallalloc churn. quant path does extra token-length bookkeeping per token which allocates more small objects. might need to reuse buffers.
alex: experiment results: defrag-1 kept RSS ~30% lower under same load, no OOMs during 30m. baseline canary still OOMing at 15% request rate.
maria: great signal. can you paste jemalloc stats from both?
alex: ```
=== jemalloc stats (baseline) ===
allocated: 12.3GB
active: 14.1GB
mapped: 16.9GB
--- tcache: many tiny bins high occupancy ---
=== jemalloc stats (defrag-1) ===
allocated: 11.9GB
active: 11.2GB
mapped: 12.0GB
```
prashant: defrag + lg_dirty_mult change seems to reduce retained pages. probable mitigation: enable aggressive defrag and tune chunk size for quant models.
maria: next steps: 1) revert quant rollout to stop impact on other pools, 2) open issue with allocation hotspots and propose buffer reuse/arena partitioning, 3) plan a rollout with allocator tuning.
alex: created issue: https://internal/issue/RED-4587 — includes heapshot, perf, jemalloc dumps. tagged @eng-runtime @eng-ml
samir: i'll follow up with a small alloc-bench PR to reproduce locally. cc @prashant for allocator review.
prashant: I'll allocate time to review tomorrow. if we want short-term we can add defrag flag to quant model variants as a stopgap.
maria: can we add a regression test in canary harness that runs long-context prompts and checks RSS growth < threshold?
samir: yes, will add a 30-min soak with synthetic long prompts. I'll send a PR.
ci-bot: PR 2134 created by samir: eng-runtime/alloc-benchmark (link: https://internal/pr/2134)
alex: thanks all — i'll keep the baseline pinned and only let defrag variants handle traffic until we have a fix. will post follow-ups in the issue. :rocket:
